title: Benji and the Homework Mystery
markdown:
Sunlight burst in! Bright, buttery. It tickled Benji's whiskers. Pigeons cooed a happy, chattering tune. Birds chirped morning greetings. A brilliant, bustling day! Benji stretched his paws. A big, satisfying yawn bubbled up, showing his strong front teeth. Time for breakfast! Crunchy bark and tasty reeds. Yum! And then… homework.

But wait! Benji’s busy nose twitched. Something felt odd. Peculiar. He padded to his workbench. Wood bits. Stone bits. All neat. There it was, just like yesterday. A smooth, grey clay tablet, cool to the touch. And on it, pressed deep into the soft clay, were the morning’s arithmetic problems. Addition, subtraction, even tricky multiplications! He could practically taste the numbers. Usually so exciting.

"Again?" Benji grumbled. Tap tap. His paw hit the tablet. "This is the third day in a row! And it looks exactly the same!" The same. Again. And again. He loved numbers. Loved building with them. Calculating perfect angles for his dams. But this felt… too much. Too familiar. Like singing the same song without a single new note. Building the exact same dam, day after day. Can you imagine? Doing the exact same thing, over and over and over? It felt a bit… pointless.

He grabbed a sharp twig. Ready to solve. But wait! He noticed something yesterday. A tiny detail that tickled his curious mind. The way the numbers were pressed in. They weren't wobbly, like his own scribbles when he was in a hurry. These were neat, deep grooves. Almost perfect. Too perfect.

"Hmm," Benji hummed, a thoughtful sound deep in his chest. His tail flicked. Thump! Puzzling. A real knotty bit of business. He looked at the tablet, then out the window towards the tallest, grandest pine tree. High up in its branches lived Star the observatory owl. Star knew everything! Especially things that were old and dusty and mysterious. Star’s knowledge was vast as the night sky!

With a determined gleam in his bright eyes, Benji zipped out of his dam. A blur of brown fur and boundless energy. He dashed across the damp grass. Thump-thump-thump! Dewdrops glittered like diamonds. The air felt cool and crisp. He bounded up the rough bark of the great pine! Claws gripped tight. Up, up, up! Eager!

"Star! Star! Are you awake?" Benji called, his voice breathy from the energetic climb, echoing through the quiet morning.

A pair of enormous, golden eyes blinked open from a cosy nook. Star the owl ruffled her magnificent, midnight-dark feathers. "Benji? What's all this commotion at this early hour?" Her voice was a soft hoot, calm and deep. She tilted her head, her gaze sharp.

"It’s the homework, Star! It’s the same, same, same! And look at this tablet!" Benji held up the clay, its surface gleaming slightly. "It’s so… pressed in! And it’s all the same numbers!"

Star glided down, landing silently. She peered intently at the tablet, her bright eyes narrowing. "Oh, my dear Benji," she hooted softly, a hint of amusement in her gaze. "This isn't new clay. Not at all! This is something much older."

"It’s not?" Benji’s ears perked up. His nose twitched with renewed curiosity. "What do you mean, Star? What *is* it?"

"This," Star explained, her voice gaining a gentle, rhythmic cadence, "is a clay tablet, just like the ancient scribes used to use, long, long ago. They would press their important messages, their stories, their numbers, into wet clay. When the clay dried hard, the writing was there forever! It's how we know so much about the brave explorers and wise builders of the past. It’s like a time capsule!"

Benji’s eyes darted back to his tablet. His beaver brain whirred. "So… someone pressed the homework *again* into *this* clay? But why is it the same? Why didn't they press new numbers?"

Star gave a wise little nod, her feathers shimmering. "Here’s where it gets truly interesting, Benji. Look very closely. Do you see how the marks are identical? Perfectly placed, perfectly deep?"

Benji squinted, his brow furrowing. He nudged the tablet closer, turning it this way and that in the bright morning sun. The marks *were* identical. Perfect little numbers, lined up neatly. Each one looked exactly like the last.

"You see," Star continued, her voice hushed with wonder, "ancient scribes were incredibly clever people! To save time, or make many copies, they discovered something absolutely amazing. They’d press their original writing into wet clay. Then, before that first piece of clay dried hard, they’d take *another* piece of wet clay and press it right onto the first one! The original writing would transfer, making a perfect, identical copy!"

"A copy!" Benji shouted, his tail thumping a happy, excited beat against the branch. "So my homework isn’t new at all! It’s just copies of old homework, pressed over and over again!" The mystery! Solved! It wasn't a mistake. It was a brilliant trick!

Star hooted with delight, a soft, happy sound. "Precisely! Someone, or perhaps something, is pressing copies of the same homework onto fresh clay each morning. A brilliant, if slightly repetitive, trick indeed!"

Benji grinned, a wide, happy beaver grin that stretched from ear to ear. The mystery was gone! Replaced by a tinkling sense of understanding and a brand-new appreciation for ancient ingenuity. He looked at his tablet with new eyes. It wasn't just homework anymore; it was a piece of history, a clever bit of ancient technology! It was a testament to the smarts of people who lived long ago.

"Wow!" Benji chirped, his voice ringing with pure joy and newfound energy. "That’s amazing! Thank you, Star! You’re the best!" He felt a burst of unstoppable energy, a brilliant, uncontainable urge to… learn more! To build new things! To tackle new problems with this same kind of clever thinking!

He scampered down the tree, his paws barely touching the ground, a happy trail of displaced bark in his wake. The sun was climbing higher, painting the world in vibrant colours – golden yellows, bright blues, and fresh greens. The morning air felt alive with promise and possibility.

"Today," Benji declared, his voice ringing with pure, unadulterated excitement, "is going to be AMAZING!"

And with a grin as wide as the river, Benji raced out the door, ready for whatever came next!
characters: Benji the beaver, Star the observatory owl
